title: Generic-component transcendence degree in a smooth local chart
statement:
Let $(A,\mathfrak m,K)$ be a nonzero commutative Noetherian local ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], let $P$ be a smooth $A$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map], and let $\mathfrak N\subset P$ be a prime with $\mathfrak N\cap A=\mathfrak m$. Set $B=P_{\mathfrak N}$, $L=\kappa(\mathfrak N)$, $F=B/\mathfrak mB$, $s=\dim F$, and $t=\operatorname{trdeg}_K L$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime, def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring, def-kun-transcendence-degree]. Let
$$r=\dim_{\mathfrak N}(\operatorname{Spec}(P\otimes_AK))$$
be the topological dimension of the closed fibre at the indicated point [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-kun-topological-dimension-at-point, def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. Then $r,s,t$ are finite nonnegative integers and $r=s+t$. For every minimal prime $\mathfrak Q$ of $P$ contained in $\mathfrak N$ whose contraction $\mathfrak p$ is a minimal prime of $A$ (minimal means containing no strictly smaller prime), put $E=\operatorname{Frac}(A/\mathfrak p)$ and $H=\operatorname{Frac}(P/\mathfrak Q)$, with the field inclusion induced by $A\to P$. The prime $\mathfrak Q$ determines a minimal prime $\overline{\mathfrak Q}$ of $P\otimes_AE$, its localization has dimension zero and residue field $H$, and
$$\operatorname{trdeg}_E H=\dim_{\overline{\mathfrak Q}}(\operatorname{Spec}(P\otimes_AE))=r.$$
Also $H\simeq\operatorname{Frac}(B/\mathfrak Q B)$ compatibly with $E$. The dimension $r$ here is the dimension at a point of a fibre, whereas $s$ is the Krull dimension of its local ring.

proof.text: Put $C_k=P\otimes_A k$ for $k=K$ or $E$. A finite presentation of the smooth algebra $P$ in particular gives finitely many algebra generators; their tensors with $1$ generate $C_k$ over $k$. Thus each $C_k$ is of finite type over its field. The affine smoothness criterion makes $f:\operatorname{Spec}P\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ smooth. The affine fibre-product isomorphism identifies its fibre over $\mathfrak m$ with $\operatorname{Spec}C_K$ and, once $E=\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ is identified in step 3, its fibre over $\mathfrak p$ with $\operatorname{Spec}C_E$.

source.place: Tag 01V6 (lemma-smooth-characterize); schemes.tex Tags 01I4/01JQ (lemma-fibre-product-affine-schemes, lemma-fibre-product-affines). Finite-type base change is written out using generators.

proof.text: The fibre prime correspondence gives the prime $\overline{\mathfrak N}$ of $C_K$ above $\mathfrak N$, with residue field $L$, compatibly with $K$. The fibre local-ring isomorphism gives $(C_K)_{\overline{\mathfrak N}}\simeq P_{\mathfrak N}/\mathfrak mP_{\mathfrak N}=F$. Apply the finite-type-over-a-field dimension formula to $(K,C_K,\overline{\mathfrak N})$. It says precisely that $r,s,t$ are finite nonnegative integers and $r=s+t$; the hypothesis $\mathfrak N\cap A=\mathfrak m$ is exactly the hypothesis needed for these fibre identifications.

For any ring $R$ and prime $\mathfrak a$, apply the localization-quotient-by-prime isomorphism to $T=R\setminus\mathfrak a$ and the maximal ideal $\mathfrak aR_{\mathfrak a}$. It identifies $\kappa(\mathfrak a)$ with the localization of $R/\mathfrak a$ at all its nonzero elements, namely $\operatorname{Frac}(R/\mathfrak a)$. Applying this to $(A,\mathfrak p)$ and $(P,\mathfrak Q)$ gives $E=\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ and $H=\kappa(\mathfrak Q)$. These identifications preserve the structure maps: the class of $a/s$ maps to $\overline a/\overline s$. Since the kernel of $A\to P/\mathfrak Q$ is $\mathfrak p$, the induced domain map $A/\mathfrak p\to P/\mathfrak Q$ is injective and its fraction-field extension is the specified inclusion $E\to H$.

source.place: Tags 00CT (proposition-localize-quotient) and 00E3 (lemma-spec-localization), applied to the complement of a prime.

proof.text: Apply the inclusion-preserving fibre prime correspondence to $A\to P$ over $\mathfrak p$. It gives a prime $\overline{\mathfrak Q}$ in $C_E$ with residue field $H$ as an $E$-field. If a prime of $C_E$ lies below $\overline{\mathfrak Q}$, its contraction lies below $\mathfrak Q$ in $P$, hence equals $\mathfrak Q$ by minimality; the bijection then makes the original prime equal to $\overline{\mathfrak Q}$. Thus $\overline{\mathfrak Q}$ is minimal. The primes of $(C_E)_{\overline{\mathfrak Q}}$ correspond to the primes of $C_E$ below $\overline{\mathfrak Q}$, so this nonzero local ring has exactly one prime. Every chain has length zero, and its Krull dimension is zero. This uses no reducedness assumption on $A$ or $P$.

source.place: Tags 00E6 (remark-fundamental-diagram), 0H9M (remark-local-ring-fibre), 00E3 (lemma-spec-localization); dimension zero directly from the definition by prime chains.

proof.text: By smooth local constancy, $d(x)=\dim_x((\operatorname{Spec}P)_{f(x)})$ is locally constant on $\operatorname{Spec}P$. Choose an open neighbourhood of $\mathfrak N$ where $d=d(\mathfrak N)$. It contains $\mathfrak Q$: indeed it contains a basic open $D(h)$ through $\mathfrak N$, and $h\notin\mathfrak N$ implies $h\notin\mathfrak Q$ because $\mathfrak Q\subseteq\mathfrak N$. Consequently $d(\mathfrak Q)=d(\mathfrak N)=r$. The affine fibre identifications of step 1 identify $d(\mathfrak Q)$ with $\dim_{\overline{\mathfrak Q}}\operatorname{Spec}C_E$.

source.place: Tag 02G1 (lemma-smooth-omega-finite-locally-free), local constancy; specialization argument using the Zariski basic opens written out.

proof.text: Apply the finite-type-over-a-field dimension formula to $(E,C_E,\overline{\mathfrak Q})$. Its local-ring dimension is zero by step 4 and its residue field is $H$, with the prescribed $E$-structure. Hence $\dim_{\overline{\mathfrak Q}}\operatorname{Spec}C_E=0+\operatorname{trdeg}_E H=\operatorname{trdeg}_E H$. Combining with step 5 gives the required equality with $r$. The same formula also proves finiteness of the generic transcendence degree.

source.place: Tag 00P1 (lemma-dimension-at-a-point-finite-type-field), applied at the minimal prime of the generic fibre.

proof.text: Finally the localization prime correspondence makes $\mathfrak QB$ a prime of $B=P_{\mathfrak N}$ contracting to $\mathfrak Q$, since $\mathfrak Q\subseteq\mathfrak N$. The localization-quotient-by-prime isomorphism identifies $B/\mathfrak QB$ with the localization of the domain $D=P/\mathfrak Q$ at the images of $P\setminus\mathfrak N$; those images are nonzero. This localization embeds in $\operatorname{Frac}D$. Conversely, its fraction field contains $D$ and the inverses of every nonzero element of $D$, so the two fraction fields coincide by their maps $a/b\mapsto a/b$. This gives $H\simeq\operatorname{Frac}(B/\mathfrak QB)$. Both maps fix $D$, hence fix $A/\mathfrak p$ and the inverses of its nonzero elements, so the isomorphism is compatible with $E$.

source.place: Tags 00E3 (lemma-spec-localization), 00CT (proposition-localize-quotient); fraction-field identification by the explicit fraction maps.
